recommendations.title: Governed KPI reporting: confidence intervals, FDR-controlled hotspots, proposed targets
recommendations.finding: Naive league tables would send the business chasing noise.
recommendations.evidence: 314 segment cells scanned: 13 have raw p<0.05 vs 16 expected by chance; 0 survive FDR (min q=0.20). Chi-square p: issue 0.33, channel 0.27, region 0.69, product 0.79, source 0.82.
recommendations.action: Publish the KPI scorecard weekly from the warehouse views with 95% CIs; flag a segment as a hotspot only if it survives FDR; agree the proposed targets with stakeholders; show rank-stability next to any ranking.
recommendations.kpi: Share of hotspot alerts that survive review
recommendations.expected_impact: Avoids mis-allocating budget to chance-driven 'hotspots'; no direct revenue claim
recommendations.confidence_basis: The finding is certain and reproducible; the benefit (fewer false alarms) is inferred, not measured

recommendations.title: Negative-feedback fast lane and service-recovery protocol
recommendations.finding: Negative-sentiment cases are resolved about twice as slowly and are far less likely to buy again.
recommendations.evidence: Negative cases take 18.1h vs 9.1h (Cohen's d=1.90); 91% of negatives breach a 12h SLA; repeat purchase 28.2% (negative) vs 72.0% (positive) = 43.8pp gap (adjusted OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.13-0.22).
recommendations.action: Score every incoming comment with the NLP sentiment model; auto-route Negative to a priority queue with a 12h resolution SLA, a named owner and a recovery playbook (apology, proactive follow-up, goodwill credit). Run it as a randomised pilot (fast lane vs control) because the data are observational.
recommendations.owner: Head of Customer Experience + Support Operations
recommendations.timeline: Pilot in 6-8 weeks; scale after a 90-day read-out
recommendations.kpi: Avg resolution time (negative cases); repeat rate (negative customers)
recommendations.expected_impact: Recoverable revenue ₹162.2K / ₹405.4K / ₹810.9K (10% / 25% / 50% of the 44pp repeat gap closed)
recommendations.confidence_basis: Association is strong and replicated (chi-square, regression, rules) but causal effect of the intervention is untested -> pilot
recommendations.caveat: Resolution time has no significant independent link to repeat purchase once sentiment is controlled (adjusted OR per SD 0.92, p=0.17); the recovery CONTACT, not speed alone, may be what matters - hence the pilot.

recommendations.title: Fix measurement foundations: timestamps, customer master, repeat-purchase definition, reason codes
recommendations.finding: The data cannot show trends, emerging issues or customer-level behaviour.
recommendations.evidence: No date field (trend / 'emerging issue' / improvement tracking impossible); 89.5% of multi-record customers have >1 region and 100% have >1 revenue value; sentiment is not clustered within customers (ICC=-0.02); 113 records have Repeat_Purchase_Flag=1 with Order_Count=1; text is 100% templated.
recommendations.action: Add event timestamps (feedback, case open/close), a stable customer key and order IDs; define Repeat_Purchase_Flag (window, post-feedback); add issue reason codes; capture real free text.
recommendations.expected_impact: Unlocks trend / early-warning KPIs and customer-level analytics (no direct revenue claim)
recommendations.confidence_basis: Fixing these gaps certainly enables the missing measurements (rule-based findings)
recommendations.caveat: Largest benefit is future measurement quality.

recommendations.title: Productionise the NLP pipeline with a human-labelled validation set and drift monitoring
recommendations.finding: Near-perfect scores reflect templated text; the model has no mechanism for unseen vocabulary.
recommendations.evidence: In-distribution accuracy 100% (CV) / 100% (hold-out); leave-one-descriptor-out accuracy 57.1% (= majority baseline 57.1%); generic VADER only 60.6% (8 of 19 opinion words score 0); on 30 hand-written natural sentences LR 70% / VADER 80% / hybrid 87% (indicative only).
recommendations.action: Collect >= 500 real comments labelled by humans for validation/retraining; adopt the hybrid (domain model + general lexicon) or a fine-tuned transformer; monitor vocabulary coverage and confidence.
recommendations.kpi: Macro-F1 on a human-labelled real-text test set
recommendations.baseline: Unknown on real text (100% on templated text)
recommendations.expected_impact: Protects every downstream KPI that depends on sentiment (no direct revenue claim)
recommendations.confidence_basis: Validation on real labelled text certainly reveals true accuracy; failure mode shown by leave-descriptor-out test
recommendations.caveat: The n=30 probe is qualitative; real validation data is the actual fix.

recommendations.title: Retention and win-back programme for high-value unhappy customers (Critical tier)
recommendations.finding: Most of the revenue at risk is concentrated in a small, identifiable group: dissatisfied records in the top half of revenue.
recommendations.evidence: At-Risk segment (K-means k=3, silhouette 0.46, bootstrap ARI 0.99): 586 records, 94% negative. Critical tier (At-Risk x revenue Q3/Q4) = 306 records carrying ₹2.65M = 72% of all Revenue at Risk; 18.4h resolution, 29% repeat.
recommendations.action: Create a named outreach list from the Critical tier; contact within 24h; tiered goodwill offers by revenue band; track save-rate. Use the NLP + segmentation flags in the warehouse (fact_feedback_segment.risk_tier) as the list source.
recommendations.timeline: List live in 4 weeks; monthly save-rate review
recommendations.kpi: Repeat rate in Critical tier; Revenue at Risk
recommendations.expected_impact: Recoverable revenue about ₹290.0K (base: 25% of the repeat gap on this tier's revenue at risk); overlaps with R2 - do not add
recommendations.confidence_basis: Segment is stable (ARI 0.99) and beats a permutation null; revenue concentration is arithmetic but the uplift is scenario-based
recommendations.caveat: Customer_ID is unstable in the source (region/revenue vary within a customer), so the list is at feedback-record level until master data is fixed (R3).

recommendations.title: Convert satisfied non-repeaters with a CRM nudge programme
recommendations.finding: A quarter of records are satisfied, quickly resolved - and still never repeat-purchase.
recommendations.evidence: 'Satisfied Non-Repeaters' = 586 records (24.4%), CSAT 3.87, resolved in 8.8h, 0% repeat, revenue ₹3.70M. Conversion of 5% / 10% / 20% would add ₹185.2K / ₹370.4K / ₹740.7K.
recommendations.action: A/B test post-purchase offers and replenishment reminders on this segment; first validate the Repeat_Purchase_Flag definition (R3).
recommendations.confidence_basis: The segment is split on a binary flag whose meaning is ambiguous (113 records conflict with Order_Count); opportunity size is a scenario
recommendations.caveat: Segment definition is partly definitional (repeat flag); treat as hypothesis.

recommendations.title: Root-cause pilots on Customer Support and App Experience (leading candidates, not proven hotspots)
recommendations.finding: These two topics lead the rankings but the gap to the average is statistically indistinguishable from chance.
recommendations.evidence: Negative rate Customer Support 28.7% and App Experience 26.2% vs 24.0% overall; issue-level chi-square p=0.33; rank #1 on Revenue at Risk in 43% / 37% of bootstrap resamples (chance 12.5%), top-3 in 86% / 83%.
recommendations.action: Read a stratified sample of negative texts per topic; run time-boxed fixes (support scripts, app checkout journey) with a pre-registered metric; do NOT re-allocate large budgets on the current ranking.
recommendations.kpi: Negative rate for the two topics (with CI)
recommendations.expected_impact: Excess negative revenue vs average about ₹129.8K - small and uncertain
recommendations.confidence_basis: Not significant (p=0.33), not FDR-significant; ranking is fragile
recommendations.caveat: Low priority until more data (or timestamps) allow a firmer test.
